races.title: State Assembly, District 71
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Kate Sanchez
cands.bio: Republican member of the California State Assembly for District 71 since December 2022. Small business owner and nonprofit executive. Former U.S. House legislative staffer, worked for the California Policy Center, and was executive director of the California Women's Leadership Association.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists the Republican Party of California and Reform California among her 2026 endorsements. The Republican Party of California also appears for 2024.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Sanchez was born or raised, or when she came to California; the only personal detail on record is a birth year of 1988. We found no statements from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, guns, abortion, school choice or teacher pay. The 'said' entry on public safety comes from her campaign site, which describes bills she says she authored; we could not check those bills against official legislative records. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or land-use stances. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member since December 2022 and re-elected in 2024. Earlier worked as legislative staff for the U.S. House and for the California Policy Center, ran a small business, and was a nonprofit executive director. Holds a B.A. with a political science/law concentration.
qual.why: Nearly four years of legislative service plus policy and legislative-staff work places her in the high band. Committee seats and the vice-chair post were not counted.
qual.label: Nearly four years of legislative service plus policy and legislative-staff work places her in the high band. Committee seats and the vice-chair post were not counted.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says she authored AB 75, which would increase shoplifting penalties for prior offenses, and AB 257, which would bar sitting, lying or sleeping on public property within 500 feet of a school, daycare, park or library.

cands.name: JJ Galvez
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for California State Assembly District 71. Born and raised in Honduras, he came to California for college and graduated from Loyola Marymount University in 2014. He built a career in technology and entrepreneurship and was appointed Treasurer of the Silverado-Modjeska Recreation and Park District. He has held no other office.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, California Young Democrats, Equality California and the California Mountain Biking Coalition are listed as endorsers, along with several Sway voting-group guides.

In his Ballotpedia survey he lists endorsements from U.S. Rep. Mike Levin, Assemblymembers Corey Jackson and Cottie Petrie-Norris, State Treasurer Fiona Ma, the Iranian American Democrats of California, and several local council members and school and college trustees. These are his own claims.

cands.gaps: We could not find the year Galvez came to California or the names of his employers and companies, so his technology and business career is known only from his own description. He has not held an elected office, so there is no voting record. We found no documented actions in office on housing, taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, policing or schools. His stated positions come only from his campaign site and Ballotpedia survey. We found no news coverage of controversies. The campaign site's 'Meet JJ' page was cut off, and some of his linked policy videos and proposals were not available to read.

local.label: Roots 40: He was born and raised in Honduras and came to California to attend college, graduating in 2014, and he now lives in Silverado Canyon, so the record shows about 12 or more years in California as an adult.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He describes a career in technology and entrepreneurship, leading teams at startups and large companies and building organizations from scratch. He was appointed Treasurer of the Silverado-Modjeska Recreation and Park District, where he says he rebalanced the budget after a 30% cut in county funding.
qual.why: He has business and management experience and a small local budget role, but no prior legislative service and no documented law or policy career. That places him in the middle band.
qual.label: He has business and management experience and a small local budget role, but no prior legislative service and no documented law or policy career. That places him in the middle band.

stop-data-centers.evidence: Says on his campaign site that data centers should not be built without community buy-in. This is a conditional position, not a ban or moratorium.

land-for-floridians.evidence: Proposes to curb speculation in housing from private equity firms and foreign cash-based investors.

clean-money.evidence: States that he does not accept corporate donations and describes his campaign as grassroots-funded.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says building affordable housing does not have to mean destroying remaining wildlands, and that clean water and air should be preserved. His site also proposes incentives for developers to build more affordable housing and deregulation to cut costs.
